title: Wired to the Sun
endLine: Signals made by light switch the cycle on; darkness switches it off.

scenes.tts: Each carbon dioxide fixed costs three A T P and two N A D P H. The light reactions pay that bill. Now the sun sets. At night, the chloroplast makes N A D P H by burning sugar. So why doesn't the loop spend it to build sugar right back?
scenes.caption: Each CO2 fixed costs 3 ATP and 2 NADPH. The light reactions pay that bill. Now the sun sets. At night, the chloroplast makes NADPH by burning sugar. So why doesn't the loop spend it to build sugar right back?
scenes.visual: Continue the first film's 16:9 chloroplast world and colour map without a reset: the thick circular conveyor fills about 65% of the frame height in a TEAL stroma; GREEN five-counter RuBP carriers circulate clockwise; BLUE carbon dioxide counters drift in; GOLD 'G3P · 3C' blocks drop into the GOLD output tray at right; the schematic Rubisco clamp sits at the top of the loop; the thylakoid bar sits along the left edge; the ATP and NADPH blocks and their two meters sit at the bottom, as in the first film. New and carried all film: a small sun disc at top right that can sink and become a moon. During the first two sentences, the thylakoid bar pulses and ATP and NADPH blocks stream into the turning conveyor; a ledger tag 'per CO2: 3 ATP + 2 NADPH' rides beside the meters, then fades. On 'the sun sets', the sun disc sinks and turns into a moon, the teal stroma dims to night blue, and the thylakoid bar stops pulsing. On 'burning sugar', a PURPLE wheel labelled 'burns sugar' rolls in at right: it takes a GOLD block from the tray and releases an NADPH block. On the question, the NADPH block drifts toward the slowed conveyor and stops halfway; a large white question mark grows over the conveyor. Stroma particles keep drifting.
scenes.narration: Each CO2 fixed costs 3 ATP and 2 NADPH. The light reactions pay that bill. Now the sun sets. At night, the chloroplast makes NADPH by burning sugar. So why doesn't the loop spend it to build sugar right back?

scenes.visual: The question mark transforms into the centred title 'Wired to the Sun' with a short gold rule beneath it, over the dimmed night world. The PURPLE wheel turns slowly; the conveyor crawls. Fade the title before the two seconds end.

scenes.tts: Suppose it did. The loop would build sugar while another pathway burns that same sugar. That is a futile cycle. So light itself flips the loop's switches, through three signals in the stroma.
scenes.visual: A dashed white frame labelled 'what if' surrounds the night world. Inside it, the conveyor speeds up: each GOLD block it makes slides from the tray straight into the PURPLE wheel, and the wheel's NADPH block slides back into the conveyor. A single circular arrow sweeps around both machines, labelled 'futile cycle', and the gold blocks visibly go round and round without piling up. On 'Suppose it did' the frame appears; on 'futile cycle' the arrow completes. On 'So light itself flips', the dashed frame dissolves, the conveyor coasts to a stop, the PURPLE wheel slides off the right edge, and the moon rises back into the sun disc as the stroma brightens to teal. At top left, a small control panel slides in with three dark toggle switches labelled '1', '2', '3'; they stay dark.
scenes.narration: Suppose it did. The loop would build sugar while another pathway burns that same sugar. That is a futile cycle. So light itself flips the loop's switches, through three signals in the stroma.

scenes.tts: Signal one starts at the thylakoid. In the light, it pumps protons from the stroma into the lumen, the space inside it. Pump after pump, protons leave the stroma.
scenes.visual: Camera glides left: the thylakoid bar enlarges into a long rounded sac filling about 60% of the frame height. Its inside is labelled 'lumen'; the teal outside is labelled 'stroma'. Sunlight rays from the sun disc strike the sac. Small WHITE dots labelled 'protons' cross the membrane from stroma into lumen through two pump icons, one stroke per beat; the lumen visibly crowds while the stroma dots thin. On the stroma side, a vertical gauge appears, labelled 'stroma pH', with a WHITE needle on a scale marked only '7' at the bottom and '8' at the top, a small 'schematic' tag beneath; the needle rests at 7. The conveyor stays visible, small, at right.
scenes.narration: Signal one starts at the thylakoid. In the light, it pumps protons from the stroma into the lumen, the space inside it. Pump after pump, protons leave the stroma.

scenes.tts: Watch the stroma as the protons go, one after another. Does the stroma's p H fall, or does it rise?
scenes.caption: Watch the stroma as the protons go, one after another. Does the stroma's pH fall, or does it rise?
scenes.visual: The pumps keep stroking and WHITE proton dots keep crossing into the lumen. A large white question card appears above the sac: 'Stroma pH: fall or rise?' A grey cover with a '?' slides over the gauge's needle so its position is hidden. Nothing else changes.
scenes.narration: Watch the stroma as the protons go, one after another. Does the stroma's pH fall, or does it rise?

scenes.visual: Predict pause. Hold the question card 'Stroma pH: fall or rise?' and the covered gauge. The pumps keep a slow steady stroke and single WHITE dots keep crossing into the lumen; no answer appears.

scenes.tts: It rises, from about seven to eight. Signal two, in the textbook account, is magnesium. Magnesium ions flow from the lumen into the stroma to balance the charge.
scenes.visual: The question card dissolves and the cover lifts: the WHITE needle climbs from 7 to 8 (timing schematic), with a tag 'about 7 → 8'. Toggle '1' on the control panel flips on and lights WHITE, its label changing to 'pH'. On 'magnesium', SILVER dots labelled 'Mg2+' leave the lumen and drift into the stroma along a dashed path, with a small tag 'textbook account' beside the path. Toggle '2' flips on and lights SILVER, its label changing to 'Mg2+'. The pumps keep a gentle stroke.
scenes.narration: It rises, from about seven to eight. Signal two, in the textbook account, is magnesium. Magnesium ions flow from the lumen into the stroma to balance the charge.

scenes.tts: Both signals act on Rubisco. A separate carbon dioxide first joins a lysine on the enzyme, forming a carbamate. The carbamate then holds a magnesium ion, and that pair builds the working active site.
scenes.caption: Both signals act on Rubisco. A separate CO2 first joins a lysine on the enzyme, forming a carbamate. The carbamate then holds a magnesium ion, and that pair builds the working active site.
scenes.visual: Camera returns to the conveyor and pushes in on the Rubisco clamp at the top of the loop until it fills about 60% of the frame height; the control panel stays small at top left. Inside the open jaw stands a short peg labelled 'lysine'. A BLUE carbon dioxide counter wearing a WHITE ring, labelled 'activating CO2', docks onto the peg; the docked pair is relabelled 'carbamate'. A SILVER 'Mg2+' dot then snaps in beside it. The pair glows and the jaw's outline sharpens and brightens, labelled 'working active site'. No atoms, bonds or molecular structure; shapes only.
scenes.narration: Both signals act on Rubisco. A separate CO2 first joins a lysine on the enzyme, forming a carbamate. The carbamate then holds a magnesium ion, and that pair builds the working active site.

scenes.tts: High p H helps the lysine react, and more magnesium completes the pair. So one carbon dioxide switches Rubisco on, and a different one gets fixed.
scenes.caption: High pH helps the lysine react, and more magnesium completes the pair. So one CO2 switches Rubisco on, and a different one gets fixed.
scenes.visual: On 'High pH', the lit 'pH' toggle pulses and the lysine peg glows; on 'more magnesium', the lit 'Mg2+' toggle pulses and the SILVER dot glows. On 'one carbon dioxide switches Rubisco on', the WHITE-ringed counter stays docked and gains the label 'switch'. On 'a different one gets fixed', a plain BLUE counter arrives with a GREEN RuBP carrier, the clamp closes, and the first film's split plays: two '3-PGA · 3C' blocks glide away along the conveyor, the plain counter riding in one of them. The ringed 'switch' counter stays in the jaw throughout.
scenes.narration: High pH helps the lysine react, and more magnesium completes the pair. So one CO2 switches Rubisco on, and a different one gets fixed.

scenes.tts: A Rubisco that is not switched on clamps onto RuBP so tightly it shuts itself down. An A T P-burning chaperone, Rubisco activase, pries the sugar loose.
scenes.caption: A Rubisco that is not switched on clamps onto RuBP so tightly it shuts itself down. An ATP-burning chaperone, Rubisco activase, pries the sugar loose.
scenes.visual: Beside the working clamp, a second, GREY clamp slides in: no ringed counter, no silver dot, labelled 'not switched on'. It snaps shut on a GREEN RuBP carrier and locks, shaking slightly; a tag reads 'stuck'. A small token labelled 'Rubisco activase' arrives carrying one ATP block; the ATP block is spent and fades, the token wedges the grey jaws open, and the GREEN carrier pops loose back onto the conveyor. The grey clamp then slides out of frame. The working clamp keeps closing in rhythm at the top of the loop.
scenes.narration: A Rubisco that is not switched on clamps onto RuBP so tightly it shuts itself down. An ATP-burning chaperone, Rubisco activase, pries the sugar loose.

scenes.tts: Signal three is the most elegant. Photosystem one, driven by light, makes reduced ferredoxin. Through a reductase, ferredoxin then makes reduced thioredoxin.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the full world: conveyor at centre, thylakoid bar at left pulsing in sunlight, control panel at top left with two lit toggles and toggle '3' still dark. On 'Photosystem one', a marker on the thylakoid bar labelled 'Photosystem I' flashes; a CYAN token labelled 'ferredoxin' leaves it. The token reaches a small turning gear labelled 'reductase', where a separate dim ORANGE token labelled 'thioredoxin' waits; the ferredoxin token dims as its electrons pass through the gear, and the thioredoxin token lights up glowing ORANGE. The ORANGE token splits into four copies that hover over the conveyor.
scenes.narration: Signal three is the most elegant. Photosystem one, driven by light, makes reduced ferredoxin. Through a reductase, ferredoxin then makes reduced thioredoxin.

scenes.tts: In four Calvin enzymes, thioredoxin breaks a sulfur-to-sulfur bridge between two cysteines. Freed, each enzyme can take its active shape. One of them spends the A T P that rebuilds RuBP.
scenes.caption: In four Calvin enzymes, thioredoxin breaks a sulfur-to-sulfur bridge between two cysteines. Freed, each enzyme can take its active shape. One of them spends the ATP that rebuilds RuBP.
scenes.visual: Four RED closed-latch icons, each marked 'S–S', sit on four stations of the conveyor: one on the reduction lane labelled 'G3P dehydrogenase', two on the shuffle drum labelled 'FBPase' and 'SBPase', one on the returning-RuBP arrow labelled 'PRK'. Each latch is a plain padlock-like icon, not a molecular structure. One ORANGE thioredoxin copy lands on each latch in turn; the latch splits into two open WHITE halves and its station snaps from a slumped outline into a crisp, brighter shape. On 'spends the ATP that rebuilds RuBP', the PRK station glows, an ATP block enters it, and a GREEN RuBP carrier rolls out onto the loop, as in the first film. Toggle '3' flips on and lights ORANGE, labelled 'thioredoxin'.
scenes.narration: In four Calvin enzymes, thioredoxin breaks a sulfur-to-sulfur bridge between two cysteines. Freed, each enzyme can take its active shape. One of them spends the ATP that rebuilds RuBP.

scenes.tts: Here is the rule. Each switch is thrown by a change that light itself makes in the stroma. So the loop builds sugar only while the light reactions run.
scenes.visual: All three toggles glow on the control panel: WHITE 'pH', SILVER 'Mg2+', ORANGE 'thioredoxin'. On 'thrown by a change that light itself makes', three thin lines draw from the sun disc to the three toggles, labelled 'made by light'. The conveyor runs at full speed: ATP and NADPH blocks stream from the pulsing thylakoid bar, the Rubisco clamp closes in rhythm with its ringed switch counter, and GOLD blocks drop into the output tray. On the last sentence, a label settles under the loop: 'runs with the light'.
scenes.narration: Here is the rule. Each switch is thrown by a change that light itself makes in the stroma. So the loop builds sugar only while the light reactions run.

scenes.tts: At nightfall, the light reactions stop, and thioredoxin is re-oxidized. The sulfur bridges reform, the enzymes switch off, and the cycle quietly stalls.
scenes.visual: The sun disc sinks into the moon and the stroma dims to night blue; the thylakoid bar stops pulsing and the ATP and NADPH streams stop. The four ORANGE thioredoxin copies dull and are relabelled 're-oxidized'. On 'bridges reform', the four RED 'S–S' latches snap closed again and their stations slump back to dim outlines. On 'switch off', toggle '3' goes dark, and toggles '1' and '2' dim with it. On 'quietly stalls', the conveyor decelerates smoothly to a stop, with the GREEN carriers and GOLD blocks resting in place; stroma particles keep drifting.
scenes.narration: At nightfall, the light reactions stop, and thioredoxin is re-oxidized. The sulfur bridges reform, the enzymes switch off, and the cycle quietly stalls.

scenes.tts: So the plant has wired its sugar factory to the sun. It builds while daylight pays the bill, and it rests through the dark.
scenes.visual: One slow day-night time-lapse in the same world. The moon rises into the sun: the three toggles light in order, the four latches open, and the conveyor spins up with GOLD blocks dropping into the tray. Then the sun sinks into the moon: the toggles go dark, the latches close, and the conveyor rests. On 'wired', the three lines from the sun disc to the toggles brighten once; the label 'wired to the sun' appears beneath the loop.
scenes.narration: So the plant has wired its sugar factory to the sun. It builds while daylight pays the bill, and it rests through the dark.

scenes.visual: End card over the dimmed world while the sun disc keeps slowly cycling to moon and back and the conveyor speeds and slows with it, so the frame never freezes. Large white text, centred: 'Signals made by light switch the cycle on; darkness switches it off.' A short gold rule beneath it. No title and no extra claim.
